subject: Infra SRE proposal: cert automation & DNS ownership for private endpoints
messages:
From: Mike L. <mike.l@acmehealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: susan.w@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoints — cert automation and zone ownership questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're the SRE team at Acme Health and are starting the production rollout of Redwood Private in our VPC. A few urgent questions from our side before we hand this off to infra:

- We currently run a split-horizon DNS setup (internal zones: acme.internal, external: acme.com). For Redwood private endpoints (internal only) do you expect us to host the internal zone and create A/CNAME records, or should Redwood provide a private zone delegation?
- For certs: we'd like automation. Our security team prefers internal CA issuance inside the VPC (no public ACME). Can Redwood's private control plane integrate with on-prem/internal PKI for issuance/rotation, or do you recommend running cert-manager with a local vault HSM?
- TLS termination: do you support TLS termination at the edge appliance inside our VPC with mTLS back to Redwood runtime, or do you require TLS passthrough to your pods?

I've attached a short inventory (acme-health-inventory.csv) showing our current DNS servers and a list of internal domains. Happy to hop on a call.

--
Mike L.
SRE, Acme Health
messages_1:
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Mike L. <mike.l@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoints — cert automation and zone ownership questions

Mike — thanks for the inventory and the clear questions. Below is a concise proposal we can iterate on; I'll summarize options and a recommended path that balances security and low operational burden. Attaching a draft playbook (redwood-private-cert-playbook.pdf) and a small diagram.

Summary (recommended):
- DNS ownership: you should continue to own the authoritative internal zones. Redwood supports two ways to resolve private endpoints: delegated private zones (we provide NS records to point to your internal resolvers) or CNAME/A records created by your DNS team. For your split-horizon setup I'd recommend the NS delegation approach — reduces accidental divergence.
- Certificate issuance: for strict internal PKI requirements, we support an internal PKI integration flow — either:
  1) Redwood uses a customer-managed certificate broker running in your VPC (we provide a lightweight agent) that fetches certs from your CA and writes them to a mountable secret store; or
  2) You run cert-manager in-cluster pointed at your internal CA/Vault HSM; our runtime picks up certs from the mounted secret path.
  Option 1 is lower lift for customers who don't want to operate cert-manager; option 2 fits teams that already automate many certs.
- TLS termination: for compliance you can terminate TLS at your edge (edge proxy) and then mTLS to our private control plane. We also support (and sometimes recommend) TLS origination at the Redwood ingress if you want our runtime to manage cert rotation entirely. The common pattern we use for regulated workloads is: terminate at customer edge -> mTLS to Redwood ingress -> internal service TLS using short-lived certs.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 60-minute design call (SRE + network + security) to align on zone delegation, cert broker option, and KMS/HSM integration.
- Post-call: Redwood will produce a one-page runbook for your infra team + a timeline for automated rotation.

Questions for you ahead of the call:
1) Do you have a preferred HSM/KMS vendor (e.g., AWS KMS w/ CloudHSM, HashiCorp Vault HSM)?
2) Are there existing CORS/ingress policies or IP allowlists we should be aware of?

Thanks — I'll schedule time once you confirm stakeholders.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
messages_2:
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 12 Jan 2027 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoints — cert automation and zone ownership questions

Adding a few technical clarifications from runtime infra side:

- Delegation details: if you go NS delegation we need the following TTLs and glue records (I list them in the attached diagram). We'll also want a short-lived test record we can lookup from our monitoring in your VPC prior to cutover.
- SAN strategy: we recommend issuing SAN certificates that cover the full set of internal hostnames Redwood will advertise rather than wildcard where possible — this makes auditing simpler with your CA policies.
- Rotation cadence: our default rotation is every 30 days for short-lived cert flows; if you prefer, we can adapt to your internal policy (e.g., 90 days) but that increases blast radius window.

I'll bring a checklist to the design call: cert provisioning API endpoints, secret mounting paths, cert watcher behavior, and example errors to expect during rotation.

- Dylan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
messages_3:
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Mike L. <mike.l@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoints — cert automation and zone ownership questions

Quick note from security:

- KMS/HSM: we have integrations tested with AWS KMS + CloudHSM and with HashiCorp Vault using an HSM-backed cluster. If Acme wants to keep private CA keys fully on-prem we can use our agent to fetch signed leaf certs only (so private keys never leave your HSM).
- Audit/logging: Redwood can emit cert lifecycle events (issue, rotate, revoke) to your SIEM over syslog or to a webhook endpoint. We'll include event schemas in the runbook.
- Mutual TLS: If you require client-auth at the edge, we need an inbound CA bundle from you so our runtime can validate client certs.

I'll also prepare a short compliance appendix describing how we handle private key custody when using the agent model.

-S
